subject.title: feat(memory-lancedb): scope memory_recall and memory_forget in a shared store

question: Should the bundled memory-lancedb plugin expose caller-supplied scopes before OpenClaw has a trusted active-context scope signal?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but implementation review cannot decide whether manual model-selected partitions with no scoped automatic recall are the permanent official product contract.

options.title: Design active-context scoping first
options.body: Pause this contract until storage, capture, recall and forget can share a typed scope derived from or validated against runtime context.

options.title: Accept manual partitions
options.body: Land caller-supplied scopes as an explicitly non-authorizing opt-in primitive and accept that scoped rows remain unavailable to automatic recall for now.

options.title: Keep scoping external
options.body: Leave multi-scope behavior to external memory plugins that own their scope propagation and authorization policies.

recommendation.title: Design active-context scoping first
recommendation.body: Pause this contract until storage, capture, recall and forget can share a typed scope derived from or validated against runtime context.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects them to bundled memory-lancedb maintenance, while this decision concerns the permanent official plugin contract rather than a mechanical implementation detail.
